_read: The one file to read to choose and fill a screen. Each blueprint: what information it is for, where its slots sit (grid areas, one letter a slot), what fills each slot, and its live reference. Slots are one of six kinds. The words in a slot always come from the approved content script; the pictures from the build sheet. The empty layouts are design/template-blueprints/index.html (scripts/blueprints.py writes it from this file).

kinds.Title: the screen's title or question - script title / question
kinds.Text: approved words that teach - script text and the template's own fields
kinds.Info: what the room reads at a glance - chips, numbers, a table, readings, a list to tick, the choices' marks
kinds.Picture: a figure with a reason (2.116.0): a photograph, a 2D-kit / 3D-kit / custom figure, or a static 3D render - build sheet figure; its kind follows its "why" (mechanism, sequence, comparison, quantity-change, spatial, real-thing-recognition, still); no picture at all when the words read on their own
kinds.Animation: something that moves by itself - a simulator screen, a clock, a meter, a flow
kinds.3D: a live 3D scene the room turns - build sheet figure (*.kit3d.json)

rules: pick by the information: the first blueprint whose 'for' matches it (script/GUIDE.md section 1 says how to write its fields)
never the same look twice in a row (L62); each picture by the picture rule (L67, course-visuals SKILL.md)
a task screen: the factory picks the Navy or the white theme so neighbouring screens do not repeat
a self-check of five: three of the richest tasks (3D, animation, a control panel), two basic (match, order, choose)

a picture beside words comes in four boxes - text-wide 40 %, even 45 %, picture-wide 58 %, picture-large 65 % of the width (layout-templates.json "boxes"): the compiler gives the picture the box its names need and the words what is left; words over that column's measured budget are split by the script into two slides or given another slide type (L61), in parts only where the script asks for it on purpose ("in_parts", at most two a module, never two in a row); a picture no box beside its words can show goes on the stage alone or is made another kind of picture (in steps, a 3D model with names on tap) - never squeezed. A build sheet may name one: "box"
slides: blueprints/ - one file a slide blueprint (<template>.<variant>.json): where its slots sit, what fills each, its shape (layout-templates.json "shapes") and what it is good for ("fits": the group of slides it can stand in for, the pictures it takes and the picture shapes its box suits, the words and their budget). The compiler, the package check and the empty catalogue read the folder: a new layout is a new file there and its CSS in gb_layouts.css
